title: Midday Kernel Gremlin: Batching & KV-cache Scrum (Apr 2-4 2029)
content:
Purpose:
- Capture the ad hoc midday scrums we ran this week after we observed recurring ~30–120ms jitter spikes in the small-batch tail (p95/p99) tied to kernel handoffs and KV-cache misses. Aim: sync hypotheses, quick experiments, and short-term mitigations that we can ship during the sprint.

Attendees:
- Jordan Ames (owner)
- Priya Narang (kernel lead)
- Devon Lee (profiling / perf tools)
- Marco Gutierrez (kv-cache & eviction)
- Elena Park (oncall, rollouts)
- brief pop-ins: R. Huang (SRE), T. Ocampo (bench)

Quick summary / tl;dr:
- Reproduced p99 tail spike locally with synthetic small-batch stream; correlated to a kernel handshake path that stashes a micro-lock for ~60–140ms when cache miss + re-fill occurs concurrently with coalescing.
- Short-term mitigations: 1) reduce kernel-handshake backoff to 2ms for small-batch fastpath; 2) add jittered prefetch for hot prefixes; 3) instrument and flip a debug flag to keep prefill traces for 24h.
- Mid-term: redesign kernel handoff to avoid mutex hold when re-filling KV for small hot prefixes; prototype non-blocking shadow-refill.

Notes / observations:
- Repro steps (Devon): small-batch generator (batch size 1–3) sending bursty requests with ~10–30ms inter-arrival produces p99 jumps.
  - p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 42ms, p99 intermittently 110–160ms.
  - When we introduced a 1ms delay in the kernel handshake path (simulating contention), p99 moves to 180–220ms.
- Trace evidence (Elena): spans show kernel.handshake -> kvcache.refill -> kernel.resume sequence. The kvcache.refill path locks an eviction mutex for the shard; under heavy concurrent misses this stalls.
- Marco: eviction hot-shard observed in customer workload (ChatAssist) where many requests hit a narrow set of token prefixes (greetings, common prompts).
- Priya: a recent optimization (PR #823) introduced a fastpath that coalesces refill + handoff; but it still takes a synchronous copy for small token sets — likely the gremlin.

Decisions made during scrums:
1) Short-term toggle: enable jittered prefetch (probabilistic, 10% of requests for hot prefixes) — safe to ship. (Owner: Marco, target: 2029-04-06)
2) Kernel handshake backoff: cap the exponential backoff to 2ms for small-batch fastpath to avoid long sleeps. (Owner: Priya, target: 2029-04-05)
3) Debug traces: enable retaining prefills/handshake traces in debug bucket for 24h across a small subset of pods. (Owner: Elena, target: 2029-04-03)
4) Add a metric kv.refill_mutex_hold_ms (histogram) and expose per-shard heatmap in console. (Owner: Devon + Observability, target: 2029-04-12)

Experiments and results (quick lab runs):
- Experiment A (prefill jitter): 12k synthetic requests, baseline p99=135ms, with prefill jitter p99=82ms, p95 down 18%. CPU overhead ~+1.8% across pods.
- Experiment B (handshake backoff cap 2ms): improved p99 to 70–95ms in multiple runs; occasional micro-regressions at p50 (1–2ms) due to increased contention — acceptable trade-off for now.
- Experiment C (non-blocking refill prototype): ran a small prototype; memory overhead for shadow-refill ~+6% and reduced refill mutex hold to near-zero, but higher transient allocations; more profiling needed.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Is jittered prefetch amplifying cold-cache churn for rarely used prefixes? Need 48h canary with metric watch.
- Interaction with Dedicated mode: customer-configured pinning/eviction may react poorly to probabilistic prefetch; add a config flag for dedicated pools.
- How does shadow-refill interact with our current KV shard placement (hot-shard may remap)? Edge-case: double-refill race if discovery path isn’t idempotent.

Action items (owner / due):
- Marco: implement jittered prefetch toggle + add unit tests; create rollout PR. (due: 2029-04-06)
- Priya: patch handshake backoff logic and write microbench harness to simulate small-batch flows; land fast-follow fix. (due: 2029-04-05)
- Devon: add kv.refill_mutex_hold_ms histogram in telemetry and wire it to console heatmap; add alert if p99 > 100ms for >5m. (due: 2029-04-12)
- Jordan (me): coordinate canary run and incident runbook update; prepare customer note draft for ChatAssist. (due: 2029-04-07)
- Elena: enable debug trace retention for 24h on canary set; collect traces and attach to ENG-2147. (done: 2029-04-03)
- SRE (R. Huang): reserve 4 canary pods in us-west2 cluster for 48h window next week (blocker: capacity approval). (due: 2029-04-08)

Blockers and risks:
- Capacity for canary pods depends on SRE approval; if delayed, we only have small scale lab runs which may not capture production shard hotspots.
- Prefetch toggle could increase token egress cost if misconfigured; finance flagged cost watch for the canary.
- Shadow-refill prototype requires native allocator tuning to avoid GC-like stalls under sustained load.

Runbook updates: (quick notes to include in incident doc)
- Symptom: p99 spike in small-batch streams with kv.refill span present.
- Short triage steps: 1) enable prefills debug bucket; 2) check kv.refill_mutex_hold_ms heatmap; 3) toggle jittered prefetch off on Dedicated pools; 4) if p99 persists, fallback route to model-variant with larger batch aggregation (configurable).

Follow-ups for next week:
- Priya + Marco: spike on non-blocking shadow-refill and memory accounting (aim to have perf numbers by 2029-04-16).
- Observability: finalize dashboard and an automatic daily report for kv.refill mutex hold distribution.
- Product: evaluate exposing a per-customer "prefetch aggressiveness" knob for Dedicated customers (work with Solutions Eng).

Loose notes / scribbles from the scrums (raw):
- "kernel gremlin" nickname stuck — use lightly in ops notes but avoid customer-facing language.
- dev note: consider per-shard refill token bucket to throttle simultaneous refills.
- thought: could we hijack existing cache-shadowing infra to stage prefetches during low-latency windows?
- customer impact model: ChatAssist likely saw 2–3% UX regressions during peak hours; reach out to CS before broad rollout.

Attachments and references:
- bench logs: /tmp/bench-midday-2029-04-02.tar.gz (Devon)
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/829 (handshake backoff)
- Jira: ENG-2147 (kv refill mutex investigation), ENG-2151 (prefetch toggle rollout)
- Confluence draft: serving-runtime/gremlin-playbook (linked above)

If you were not at the scrums and want to dig in: start with the synthetic reproducer (linked in PR #829) and the dev traces in the debug bucket. Please ping in #serving-runtime if you want access to canary traces.

End of notes.

-- Jordan
